subject: fringe-lipped bat
title: This Bat Barely Moves All Night and Still Out-Hunts a Lion

scenes.text: This bat barely moves all night, and still out-hunts a lion.
In Panama, scientists fitted twenty fringe-lipped bats with tiny backpacks that recorded sound and movement.
The bats spent about eighty-nine percent of the time hanging still, just listening in the dark.
Then a strike. The typical hunting flight lasted eight seconds, and about half the attacks ended in a kill.
Lions win about fourteen percent of their hunts. Polar bears, about two.
Some prey weighed nearly as much as the bat. It isn't lazy. It's waiting.

description:
Tiny biologging backpacks on 20 wild fringe-lipped bats in Panama showed they spend about 89 percent of their time perched, listening, with a median hunting flight of just 8 seconds.
About half of their attacks succeed, compared with about 14 percent for lions and 2 percent for polar bears, and some prey, like gladiator tree frogs, weigh nearly as much as the bat.
Which predator would you bet on?
first_comment: One bat kept chewing a single catch, on and off, for 84 minutes. Dragonflies and porpoises still beat it, at over 90 percent. Which hunter surprises you most?
